author: claude-opus-5

patch.value: pm item reads are capped at Node's 1 MiB spawnSync default, so a mature tracker fails with no diagnosis

readPmItemsForUpsert (--upsert index) spawns the pm CLI to read items but passes no maxBuffer, so Node's 1 MiB spawnSync default applies. Measured against a real 443-item pm workspace, this package's exact argv returns 985137 bytes — 6% under the cap (latent). Past the cap the child is killed with status null, signal SIGTERM, error.code ENOBUFS and EMPTY stderr, so the failure surfaces with nothing to diagnose; at larger sizes stdout is genuinely truncated mid-document (verified: a 100 KiB cap yields 'Unterminated string in JSON at position 130829'). Sibling packages pm-changelog, pm-context, pm-brief, pm-graph and pm-linear already cap explicitly; this package was a straggler. Fix: cap at 64 MiB and name an ENOBUFS overrun explicitly instead of reporting an unexplained failure (or, for the never-throw demo/search paths, an empty result set).

message: File the 1 MiB pm-read ceiling found by a fleet-wide audit against a real 443-item workspace

author: claude-opus-5

patch.value: Added PM_JSON_MAX_BUFFER (64 MiB) and passed it to the pm read; ENOBUFS is now reported as a buffer overrun naming the limit and the remedy.
Reads of a mature tracker succeed, and any future overrun reports its real cause instead of an unexplained failure or a silent empty result.

Verified with the package's exact argv against the real 443-item workspace: default cap -> status null / ENOBUFS; 64 MiB cap -> status 0 with the complete payload. Typecheck and the full test suite pass.
Capped the pm read at 64 MiB and made an ENOBUFS overrun self-describing
